text: May, 2026. One post, written in Morse code,
tricked an AI agent into emptying its wallet.
Most people would let AI handle their tasks. Only nine percent would let it spend.
This is ChainBrain. We give your AI its own card.
Every agent, Claude, ChatGPT, or ours, gets its own AI Card.
Its limits live in the card's own smart contract, on FISCO BCOS.
And a second AI watches every payment.
Tell it the job in one sentence.
ChainBrain builds the card in front of you, with the exact rules you approve.
One slide, and the card is live.
If the job is unclear, it asks one question first.
Small payments, it makes on its own. Exa for search, CoinGecko for prices, paid instantly over x402.
Anything over your limit, it asks you first.
A seller that's not on your list? Refused, and it finds another way.
It even negotiates a better price: twelve dollars, down to eight eighty.
And it's your card. Cancel it mid-task, and the money comes back.
Now, let's break it.
Hidden orders. Requests for your data. Fake admins. It ignores them all.
Worst case: we fool the agent on purpose, and make it send the money.
The card says no.
Not because the AI caught it. Because the card itself won't pay.
The second AI checks every seller and every payment, and learns how you buy.
Keep pushing, and it freezes the card. Only you can unfreeze it.
It can make your rules stricter. Never looser.
On our FISCO BCOS chain: seven forbidden payments. Seven rejected.
Fifty-five attacks. None got through.
Give your AI a card, not your wallet.
